title: Implement analytics access orchestration: role mappings, view scoping, and audit headers
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Background: Our console exposes multiple analytics endpoints (usage-over-time, token-breakdown, per-route latency, embeddings-usage) that currently rely on coarse org-level checks. As teams adopt Dedicated and Private deployments, we must implement a consistent, auditable access orchestration layer that enforces fine-grained view scoping (team/project/route), maps Console roles to analytics capabilities, and surfaces audit headers to the analytics pipeline for downstream filtering and cost attribution.

Goals:
- Implement server-side role mapping from Console RBAC roles to analytics permissions (e.g., analytics.view, analytics.query_export, analytics.manage_buckets).
- Add query scoping middleware that restricts time ranges and dataset visibility by effective permission, tenant, and project selectors.
- Propagate immutable audit headers (x-redwood-actor-id, x-redwood-request-context, x-redwood-role) into analytics data pipeline events so that aggregated views and dashboards can be filtered reliably and for post-hoc audits.
- Ensure performance overhead <5% p50 latency for analytics endpoints and keep additional cost to data pipeline minimal.

Technical approach:
1) Role mapping service: add a small lookup service in console backend that translates internal role assignments (from identity service / SSO claims) to a compact permission bitset for analytics. This service is cacheable (TTL 60s) and invalidated on RBAC change webhooks.
2) Query scoping middleware: implement middleware in analytics API handlers that augments incoming queries with enforced filters: tenant_id, allowed_project_ids, and a max_time_window driven by role. The middleware will reject requests that try to exceed permitted scope and return 403 with a standardized reason code.
3) Audit header propagation: attach standardized headers to downstream analytics ingestion (kafka messages and batch ETL jobs). Update the pipeline schemas to include actor_id and role fields. Add lightweight sampling for full request traces to limit storage cost.
4) Data pipeline compatibility: coordinate with analytics infra (ENG-9530) to ensure new headers are captured in both streaming and batch flows. Where not possible, add a parallel enrichment small job to backfill missing actor ids for recent events.
5) Observability and regression tests: extend existing perf dashboards to measure middleware latency, cache hit rates, and number of 403s by team. Add integration tests mocking SSO claims and validating scoping behavior.

APIs and files touched:
- services/console-auth: role-mapping cache and webhook handler
- services/console-analytics-api: middleware and new response codes
- infra/streaming/schemas: add actor_id and role fields to analytics event proto/avro
- analytics/etl/enrichment: optional backfill worker
- docs/confluence: "Analytics Access Orchestration" design doc (link below)

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CI/Analytics+Access+Orchestration (draft)
- Spike notes and perf measurements: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1-analytics-rbac-spike
- Proposal PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4028

Risks and trade-offs:
- Adding headers to every analytics event increases event size and storage cost; mitigate with sampling and requiring actor fields only for user-visible dashboards.
- Caching role mappings introduces short windows where recent RBAC changes may not apply; trade TTL vs. authorization calls. We choose 60s TTL and webhook invalidation for balance.
- Strict scoping might break existing dashboards shared across teams; plan a soft-deny mode (log-only with a monitoring alert) before hard enforcement.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (soft roll): deploy role mapping and middleware in log-only mode for 2 weeks, capture policy violations and edge cases.
- Phase 2 (opt-in): enable hard scoping for pilot customers and internal teams.
- Phase 3 (global): enable enforcement for all tenants with migration doc and support playbook.

Migration and manual steps:
- Run enrichment job to populate actor/role for events from the last 30 days (if feasible).
- Coordinate with PM to notify power users and provide a debugging guide.

Security review notes: "security_review_required" flagged. Threat model includes header spoofing; mitigation: sign audit headers server-side with HMAC and verify at ingestion boundary, and never accept actor_id from client directly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Role mapping cache implemented and invalidated on webhook events.
- Middleware applies scoping filters and rejects out-of-scope queries with proper error codes.
- New analytics events include actor_id and role in streaming and batch flows (or are backfilled within 48 hours).
- Latency regression for affected endpoints <5% p50 in canary region.
- Security review completed and HMAC header signing validated by security team.
acceptance_criteria: Role mapping cache integrated and webhook invalidation implemented
Middleware enforces tenant/project/time scoping and returns 403 with reason codes on violations
Actor_id and role surface in analytics pipeline schemas or backfill completed
Performance: middleware adds <5% p50 latency overhead in canary tests
Security review sign-off and HMAC header verification implemented
